extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff, Technology Center (TC) quality assurance staff, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for deciding, handling, coordinating, and concluding ex parte reexamination proceedings (including interactions with litigation, reissue applications, PTAB proceedings, and issuance of reexamination certificates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge or stay reissue and reexamination proceedings — timing and standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to merge a reissue application and a reexamination proceeding, or to stay one because of the other, should be filed before an order granting reexamination is issued; petitions filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will not be considered and will be returned. The patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or to stay at the time the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 is filed or thereafter. A third party requester does not have standing to petition to merge with a reissue application, but may file a notification of concurrent proceedings pursuant to MPEP § 2282 and may petition to stay the reexamination it requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent premature filings relating to the reexamination proceeding; returned petitions will be made of record in both files but no copy retained. Petitions filed by parties other than the patent owner to merge a reexamination with a reissue will be returned (or expunged if entered) as improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g). All petitions to merge or stay filed after the date of the order for reexamination are referred to OPLA for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged, if a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time fee, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid for the merged proceeding(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one appeal brief fee is required even though copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding. As to excess claim fees, reissue practice controls. Follow merged-proceeding fee treatment when proceedings are merged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of reexamination requests tied to court-ordered or stayed litigation — expedited processing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ex parte reexamination request indicates it was filed as a result of a court order or an agreement by parties to litigation sanctioned by a court, or that litigation is stayed for filing reexamination, the request will be taken up by the examiner for decision 6 weeks after filing and the proceeding will be expedited to the extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedite the reexamination and the examination following the patent owner statement and requester reply. Office actions will normally set a 1-month shortened statutory period for response (instead of the usual 2 months); response periods may be extended only upon a strong showing of sufficient cause. Actions on such proceedings generally take precedence over other examiner actions. See MPEP § 2241 and § 2263–2265 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of existing federal court decisions at time of determination on request
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Federal Court decision on the merits is known to the examiner at the time the determination on the ex parte reexamination request is made, the Office will follow guidelines recognizing that a court decision does not necessarily preclude a substantial new question (SNQ) of patentability; the Office makes an independent determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because courts and the Office use different standards of proof and claim interpretation (e.g., clear-and-convincing in court vs. preponderance in the Office), a court decision is not controlling. Deference may be accorded to factual findings of the court where the evidence is the same, but the Office independently determines SNQ. Non-final holdings of invalidity or unenforceability are not controlling; a final holding of invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office such that those claims would not present an SNQ. Any determination made after a court decision must be reviewed by the CRU Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS). See cases cited (e.g., In re Zletz, In re Etter, Ethicon v. Quigg, In re Swanson, Translogic, Trans Texas, Baxter) and MPEP § 2242.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory 3‑month decision requirement and patent owner notification duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for ex parte reexamination must be decided (grant or denial) within three months of filing (35 U.S.C. 302). Where reexamination is ordered prior to a Federal Court decision, the determination on the request will be made within that 3‑month statutory period based on the record before the examiner. The patent owner is required by 37 CFR 1.565(a) to notify the Office of any prior or concurrent proceeding or of any subsequent court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not await a court decision when making the statutory determination; if a court decision later issues, follow guidelines for review. The patent owner's duty to promptly notify the Office of any federal court decision is emphasized so the Office can review whether an SNQ still exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of subsequent federal court decisions on ongoing reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Federal Court decision issues while a reexamination is pending (or the Office becomes aware of such decision), the order to reexamine is reviewed to determine if a substantial new question of patentability still exists. A non-final court decision has no binding effect. A final court decision upholding validity does not bind the Office (the Office may continue reexamination), but a final holding of invalidity or unenforceability after all appeals is binding and claims held invalid/unenforceable will be withdrawn from reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no SNQ remains, the reexamination is terminated by the CRU or TC Director. If some claims were held invalid, use form paragraph 22.20 (Claims Held Invalid By Court, No Longer Being Reexamined) to state which claims are not being reexamined and why, with bracketed instructions for inserting specifics. If all claims being examined are finally held invalid/unenforceable, the reexamination will be vacated or terminated as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner litigation search, review, and reporting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must conduct a reasonable investigation to determine whether the patent has been or is involved in litigation, including reviewing the reexamination file, the patent file, and the results of the litigation computer search by the STIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner discovers litigation or a federal court decision at any time during the reexamination, the fact must be brought to the attention of the CRU SPRS or the TC Quality Assurance Specialist (QAS) prior to further action. The CRU SPRS or TC QAS must review any examiner action in such circumstances to ensure current Office litigation policy is followed. See MPEP § 2240.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with PTAB Review Proceedings (AIA) during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Leahy‑Smith America Invents Act (35 U.S.C. 315(d) and 325(d)), if an inter partes review, post grant review, or covered business method review (a PTAB Review Proceeding) for the same patent is before the Office, the Director may determine whether to stay, transfer, consolidate, or terminate the matters. If an examiner becomes aware of such a PTAB proceeding for the same patent being reexamined, the reexamination must be referred to the examiner’s SPRS who will coordinate with the PTAB before taking any action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination with PTAB is required before further action on the reexamination. Note that the statutory requirement to decide a reexamination request within three months still applies despite PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) and requirements for reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of the ex parte reexamination, the examiner must prepare a NIRC (form PTOL‑469) and, where claims are found patentable, provide reasons for each claim found patentable. The examiner must also prepare the reexamination file so the Office of Data Management can prepare and issue a certificate per 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner’s amendment may also be prepared where appropriate. After preparing the NIRC and attachments and completing the Examiner Checklist (PTOL‑1516), files are forwarded to CRU support staff for processing and eventual mailing/forwarding to OPLA and the Office of Data Management. Changing the patent title requires an examiner’s amendment; titles should be corrected early in prosecution. Amendments or papers filed after prosecution terminated require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing NIRC — when required and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review conference (with the CRU SPRS/TC QAS convening conferees) must be held when a NIRC is about to be issued so the conferees review the patentability of the claims; the NIRC is signed by the examiner and initialed by two or more conferees. Exceptions: a panel is not held for any claim that was in the case at the time the case was reviewed by the Board or a federal court, nor is a panel review required where the proceeding is concluded by cancellation of all claims (NIRC issuance in that instance is ministerial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conferees initial even if one dissents. If the conference does not confirm the examiner’s decision, the examiner must reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action rejecting the unconfirmed claims. Examples provided illustrate when claims previously before the Board/court are excluded from panel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rules for claims to be printed on certificate/Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting representative claim(s) for printing on the certificate cover sheet and in the Official Gazette, the broadest claim should be selected. Examiners should ordinarily designate but one claim per invention (up to five where multiple inventions exist); in reexamination, the examiner must select only one claim for publication. A dependent claim should not be selected unless the independent claim it depends on is also printed. If a dependent patent claim is selected where the original independent patent claim has been canceled, the dependent claim may be printed while the independent is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recording selection: write the claim number clearly in black ink; separate multiple claim numbers with commas; refer to claims by renumbered patent claim numbers rather than original application claim numbers. In reissue applications, select the broadest claim with changes or the broadest additional reissue claim for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner and clerk checklist items when preparing case for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publication of the certificate, the examiner must review the reexamination and patent files to ensure all appropriate parts are completed, including: IFW Search Notes (classes/subclasses searched), IFW jacket form (Litigation Review and Copending Office Proceedings boxes), Bibliographic Data Sheet correctness, Issue Classification IFW form (status and final claim numbers, international/U.S. classification), and designation of a representative claim for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Examiner Checklist (PTO‑1516) and forward to Office of Data Management. CRU support staff will complete Reexamination Clerk Checklist (PTO‑1517) and check for changes in title, inventor, assignee, continuing data, foreign priority, attorney address, and requester’s address; ensure proper entry in PALM. If patent owner requests attorneys' names printed on certificate, a separate paper explicitly requesting printing must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when all claims in the reexamination are canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: If all live claims in the reexamination are to be canceled (e.g., patent owner failed to timely respond or Board affirmed all rejections and appeal windows expired), the examiner should telephone the patent owner to verify whether a timely filing was made. If none, the examiner proceeds to issue a NIRC terminating prosecution and attaches an examiner's amendment canceling all live claims and explaining why the claims are canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two example explanatory statements are provided (failure to timely respond; Board decision affirmed and no timely appeal). The telephone interview, if made, should be made of record. To physically cancel live claims, place brackets around claims on a printed copy of the claims from the file history and scan into IFW file history. Designate a canceled original patent claim for printing in the Official Gazette (Issue Classification IFW form). No panel is required when all claims are canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple dependent claims for NIRC classification and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a multiple dependent claim is altered such that its dependency chain changes, the addition of a claim of multiple dependency is viewed for NIRC purposes as adding a new claim (i.e., new subject matter is now protected). For the Examiner’s checklist, the addition or deletion of a multiple dependency claim is viewed as amending the claim because of how claims are printed on the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: adding a multiple dependency that references a new claim (claim 2/8) is treated as a 'new claim' for purposes of classification, while the original subject matter (claim 2/1) remains 'confirmed.' Complete NIRC Part 1(h) and Examiner’s checklist (PTO‑1516) to reflect confirmed, amended, canceled, and new claims (examples in the text show mapping such as 'Patent claims confirmed: 1, 2/1, 5, 7' and 'New claims patentable: 2/8, 4/8, 6/8, 8'). For printing on the certificate, the amended form of the claim is what appears.
